beats.narration: Checkpoint one: a supposedly reusable code-review agent with one defect hiding in it. If you haven't found and fixed it, pause here and do that first.

The defect is the repo path — a specific customer's repository, hardcoded where a parameter belongs. The fix moves it into the function signature, so the next engagement passes its own path and configures the asset instead of editing the loop. Notice what stays put: the model, the prompt, the tools — that's the reusable core. Not every value becomes a parameter. Only the ones that change per customer.

elements.code:
repo_path="/home/acme/checkout-service"   # ✗ hardcoded

def build_review_agent(repo_path):        # ✓ parameter
    ...
    repo_path=repo_path,   # set per engagement

elements.text:
parameterize what CHANGES per customer —
keep the core fixed

beats.narration: That's the whole packaging test in one question: could a stranger configure this without reading the loop? Next: contributing back.
